# Terminal 1.0.51

**Signing out and switching accounts**
- Sign out and Switch account no longer close the terminal: you go straight back to the sign-in window.
- "Sign out" ends your session on the server and keeps your account number for next time. "Sign out and forget this computer" removes it too.
- You stay signed in after closing the terminal only when "Remember me" is ticked.
- Switch account lists your other accounts. Pick one and sign in; your current account stays open until the new one is signed in.

**Two-step sign-in**
- The code step has a Back button. If the code expires, you are told so and sent back to sign in.

**Starting without a connection**
- If the terminal can't reach the server that checks this installation, it still starts for up to 7 days after its last successful check. The sign-in page shows when that was.

**Also**
- You can cancel while your session is being resumed.
- Updates ask before restarting: restart now, when you close, or not now.
- Your settings are saved safely with a backup copy, so a damaged file no longer resets them.
- Chart and one-click settings saved from the terminal no longer reset your web trader preferences.

Your layout, settings and saved sign-in are kept.

# Terminal 1.0.50

**Orders you can't place are explained before you click**
- If an order would push your account into margin call, the buy or sell button is disabled and the ticket shows the exact figures, for example "Not enough free margin: needs 1,000.07 USD, available 400.00 USD". Orders that reduce your margin, such as a hedge, stay allowed.
- If your account or a symbol is buy-only or sell-only, the other side is disabled with the reason.

**Slippage**
- Your "Slippage max" setting is used exactly as you type it. Before, it was sometimes raised automatically.
- It now applies to closes too. Your broker may set a lower limit, and the lower of the two always applies.
- The F9 order window keeps its own slippage setting.

**Chart**
- Right-click orders offer buy limit/stop against the ask price and sell limit/stop against the bid.
- Orders and alerts placed from the chart appear in the Log and their tab at once.

**Positions**
- Stop loss / take profit can be sent again after a cancelled or failed change.
- A position whose close is waiting for the dealer can't have its stop loss / take profit edited.
- The Modify window no longer overwrites what you are typing.

**Always up to date**
- Balance, orders, order history, trade history and the Log refresh on their own, including after a reconnect.
- The Balance tab is filled when you sign in.

Your layout, settings and saved sign-in are kept.

# Terminal 1.0.49

**Currency conversion**
- Profit/loss, equity, margin, margin level, the margin an order needs and the point value are now converted to your account currency, exactly as the server calculates them.
- This matters for symbols not quoted in your account currency, such as USDJPY, EURGBP, CADJPY, GER40, JPN225 or UK100, and for accounts in EUR, GBP or other currencies.
- Figures are shown in your account currency (for example "P/L (EUR)", "Equity EUR").
- If a conversion price is not available, the figure shows "–" instead of a wrong number.

**Market hours**
- The weekly close and reopen follow the US clock change: markets close Friday 21:00 UTC and reopen Sunday 21:00 UTC in summer, and 22:00 UTC in winter.

Your layout, settings and saved sign-in are kept.

# Terminal 1.0.48

**Faster order confirmation**
- New positions, closes and stop loss / take profit changes appear on the chart and in the trade list as soon as the server confirms them. The terminal no longer reloads the whole list first.
- The fill sound plays at once. The log shows how long each trade took, for example "market buy 0.01 XAUUSD at 4456.73 done in 180 ms".

**Charts while the market is closed**
- The chart no longer adds empty candles while a market is closed or the price feed is quiet. A candle is only drawn from a real price, and a gap stays a gap until trading resumes.
- When the market is closed, the candle countdown shows "Market closed".
- The Sessions clock above the trading sessions now shows the current time.

Your layout, settings and saved sign-in are kept.

# Terminal 1.0.47

**Live broker changes**
- Changes your broker makes to spreads, commission, swaps, symbols, trading hours or trading halts reach the terminal within about a second. You don't need to restart or sign in again.
- The buy price shown in the ticket, one-click trading and Market Watch is the price you are filled at, including fixed-spread symbols.

**Trading halted / Close-only**
- When your broker halts trading or sets close-only, the ticket and one-click buttons are disabled and a notice explains why. You can still close positions in close-only.

**Margin call**
- A margin call or stop-out is logged with a sound, and your account panel updates at once.

**Chart and positions**
- Stop loss and take profit tags on the chart show the profit or loss at that level, for positions and pending orders.
- Positions show the move in points, and the ticket shows the point value ($).

Your layout, settings and saved sign-in are kept.

# Terminal 1.0.46

**Pending orders**
- Buy/sell limit and stop orders are now triggered by the server, so they fill even when the terminal is closed.
- If the server can't fill a pending order (for example, not enough free margin), the log shows it once with the reason, and you hear one alert.

**Account**
- The account panel shows your Stop-out level (%) beside the margin call level, and warns you when your margin level reaches either.

**Chart**
- Right-click Buy/Sell Limit and Stop orders now use the volume in your order ticket. They were always sent as 0.01 lots before.

**Market Watch**
- Ask and spread show the price you actually buy at, the same as the order ticket.

Your layout, settings and saved sign-in are kept.

# Terminal 1.0.45

**Hedged positions use less margin**
- When your broker enables hedged margin for a symbol, a BUY and a SELL on the same symbol offset each other. The account panel's margin, free margin and margin level now show that reduced margin, exactly as the platform counts it for margin calls and stop-outs.
- Nothing changes for symbols where your broker has not enabled it.

Your layout, charts, settings and saved sign-in are kept.

# Terminal 1.0.44

**Close By**
- Right-click a position, then choose **Close by**. It lists every opposite position on the same symbol. The two close against each other at one price, so you pay the spread once. If the volumes differ, the rest stays open on the larger position.

**Your chart belongs to your account**
- Indicators and drawings are now saved per account. A new account starts with a clean chart and never picks up another account's indicators or drawings on the same PC.
- Your current indicators and drawings stay with the first account you sign in with after this update.
- The session map is off by default on a new account; you can switch it on from the chart settings.

**Account changes show up at once**
- When your broker changes your leverage, account group, pricing or allowed symbols, the terminal updates straight away, without signing in again.

Your layout, settings and saved sign-in are kept.

# Terminal 1.0.41

**History: profit and loss at the end of the row**
- **Profit / Loss** is now the **last** column on the History tab, where a result belongs. **Closed** takes the slot it used to sit in, so the row reads open, close, costs, then the number you are looking for.

**History: Reason is off by default**
- The **Reason** column is no longer shown. It repeated what the close price and the S/L and T/P columns already tell you, and on a row carrying both an opening and a closing it was not clear which one it described.
- It is still there when you want it: right-click any History heading and tick **Reason**. Your choice is remembered, and the statement export still carries a Reason column as before.

**Close buttons sit with the tabs**
- **Close profit**, **Close loss** and **Close all** have moved onto the tab row itself, at the end, instead of a second strip underneath: the panel gets that row of height back for your trades.
- **Close profit** is now green and **Close loss** red, so the colour says which side of the book each one takes off. Close all stays red.

**Order type on the buttons**
- The **New order** window (F9, or a double-click on a symbol) now captions its buttons with the order type, the way the docked ticket already did: **Sell limit / Buy limit**, **Sell stop / Buy stop**. It said a plain Sell / Buy whatever type you picked.

Nothing else changed in this build. The dock's column fitting, the calendar range and everything else are as they were in 1.0.40.

# Terminal 1.0.40

**Columns fit the panel**
- Every table in the panel — Trade, Pending, Orders, History, Balance and Log — now spreads its columns across the full width of the panel, so nothing is squeezed and no space is left empty on the right. Widen the window or the panel and the columns follow.
- If you had dragged a column narrower in an earlier build and a value was showing half cut, that is gone: the fit starts from the width each column needs.
- Drag a column edge and that table keeps your widths from then on; right-click a heading for **Fit columns to width** to hand it back, or **Reset columns** to start over.

**History: S/L and T/P**
- Closed trades now show the **S/L** and **T/P** they carried when they closed, after the open and close prices. The level that closed the trade is coloured like the close price.

**History: pick dates on a calendar**
- **Custom** range: the From and To boxes each have a calendar. Click the day; typing the date still works. Days after today cannot be picked.
- Pressing Enter in the date boxes had no effect in earlier builds; the range now applies the moment a day is chosen.
- The right-click menu on the History rows (statement period, columns) now opens; it did nothing before.

**Buttons look like buttons**
- **Close profit**, **Close loss** and **Close all** are now bordered buttons with a hover state instead of bare text. Close all is marked in red.
- The same for the History range chips (the active one is filled), **Statement**, the accept / reject buttons on a requoted order, the cancel on a pending order, and the small chart controls (indicator settings, drawing settings and delete, collapse of the one-click panel).

Market Watch, the chart and the order ticket are otherwise as they were in 1.0.39.

# Terminal 1.0.39

**Tabs open instantly**
- The first time you opened **Orders** or **History** after starting the terminal, the panel could freeze for several seconds while every row in your account was laid out at once. Each table now only builds the rows on screen, so the first open takes the same instant as every later one, however long your history is.
- **Orders** now shows your newest 500 orders. Older ones will become reachable from the tab in a later build.

**Columns are divided**
- Every table in the panel — Trade, Pending, Orders, History, Balance and Log — now draws a line between columns as well as between rows, so a value is never read against the wrong heading. The lines follow your column widths when you resize or hide columns.
- The line between rows has been toned down to a normal weight. 1.0.37 and 1.0.38 made it heavier than it needed to be; the problem was the missing column lines, not the row line.

Nothing else changed in this build. Market Watch, the chart and the order ticket are as they were in 1.0.38.

# Terminal 1.0.37

**History — the closed-trades columns read correctly**
- The order is now **Ticket · Opened · Symbol · Side · Lots · Open price · Close price · Swap · Comm · Profit / Loss · Reason · Duration · Closed**.
- **Opened** and **Closed** are the times; **Open price** and **Close price** are the prices. They used to be called *Opened / Closed / Open / Close*, with the two times sitting together near the front and their matching prices five columns further along — four columns, two near-identical names. Nothing was ever filled into the wrong column, but it could not be read that way.
- The closing time now ends the row, after Duration.

**History — right-click**
- Right-clicking a row opens the **statement period** — Last day, week, month, 3 months, **6 months**, All time, Custom range — with a tick beside the one currently applied, so the menu says which window you are looking at as well as changing it.
- **Columns…** is on the same menu. It was previously only reachable by right-clicking the header.
- **6 months** is new; the toolbar had 1D / 1W / 1M / 3M / ALL / CUSTOM and skipped it.

**Market Watch**
- The Market Watch moves into the shared UI library so the terminal and the backoffice dealing desk run the same control. No change to how it looks or behaves here — the same symbol search, add and remove, spread column and category grouping — but a change fixed in one place is now fixed in both.

**Rows are easier to follow**
- The horizontal line between rows was close enough to the panel colour to disappear in some lighting. It is a little stronger in both the dark and light themes, across every table.

# Terminal 1.0.36

**Closing positions on a dealer-managed account**
- When your account is in dealer mode, a close is now sent to the dealer for review instead of executing at once. The position row shows **CLOSE · AWAITING DEALER** (or **CLOSE 0.40 REQUOTED @ … · see PENDING**) and its other actions are held until the dealer answers.
- **CANCEL** on that row withdraws the close request after a confirmation; the position stays open.
- The PENDING tab lists a queued close as **CLOSE #ticket**, so it can be tracked like any pending order.
- Close all / close by profit or loss / partial close on a dealer-managed account report **submitted · awaiting dealer review** in the LOG; nothing is dropped locally.
- Reverse never opens the opposite side while a close is awaiting the dealer.
- A cancelled pending order now shows its reason (for example **position closed by take profit**).

# Terminal 1.0.35

**General**
- **Single instance**: launching the terminal while it is already running brings the open window to the front instead of starting a second copy.

**Orders**
- Every rejection now shows its real cause. A gold / silver order during the daily settlement break (the 17:00 New York hour, Mon–Thu) says **"market is closed, opens 22:00 UTC"** instead of a feed message; a genuine feed gap during open hours says so, with the time of the last tick.
- Not enough margin shows the numbers: **"not enough free margin — need 123.45, have 20.00"**; a balance that cannot cover the order at all says **"insufficient balance — need …, balance …"**.
